The function $g(x)$ is defined on $(-\infty ,\infty ).$
The graph of the second derivative $y={g}^{″}(x)$ of the function $g(x)$ intersects the $x$-axis at the points $x=-4,$ $x=-2,$ $x=0,$ $x=2,$ and $x=4,$ as shown above. The intervals on which the function $g(x)$ is concave up are

worked_solution:
A function $g(x)$ is concave up over an interval $(a,b)$ if ${g}^{″}(x)>0$ for all $x\in (a,b).$

On the given graph of $y={g}^{″}(x)$, we can see that ${g}^{″}(x)>0$ on the intervals $(-\infty ,-4),$ $(-2,0),$ and $(2,4).$ 

Therefore, the function $g(x)$ is concave up on the intervals 

$$
(\,-\infty ,-4\,),\,(\,-2,0\,),\,(\,2,4\,).
$$
